# Requirement catalogue (PRD v2, verbatim)

Requirement IDs are stable and must be used in tickets, tests and release notes (PRD v2 §04). `ADDED v2` marks requirements that no earlier source had. `DESIGN NEEDED` marks screens with no design yet (N-xx).


## P0 · Foundation and safety

- **Weeks:** Weeks 1–3 · **Release:** R0 · Internal platform
- **Delivered to:** Founder and clinical advisor (staging, synthetic data only)
- **Day one:** Sign in with MFA, invite a colleague, see role-based navigation and walk the six end-to-end journeys on staging.
- **Goal:** A secure, deployable base that every later phase builds on, and clinical sign-off that the core flows are right before code depends on them.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Screens | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P0-01** | **Repository and delivery.** .NET 10 solution (ASP.NET Core API + BFF, React web apps), EF Core 10 migration bundles, Docker Compose with SQL Server locally. GitHub Actions runs build, .NET analyzers, unit and integration tests (Testcontainers), CodeQL, dependency and secret scanning on every pull request. Protected main; deploys only from tags. | MUST | — |  |
| **P0-02** | **Azure environments as code.** Bicep for dev, staging and production in the launch country: App Service (Linux, .NET 10), Azure SQL Database behind a private endpoint with public access disabled, private Blob Storage, Key Vault with purge protection, Application Insights, Defender for Cloud. Budgets and cost alerts per environment. OIDC federation from GitHub; no stored cloud secrets. | MUST | — |  |
| **P0-03** | **Identity.** Sign-in, MFA (TOTP and passkeys), recovery, idle timeout on shared clinic PCs, device/session revocation, invite acceptance. | MUST | F-03, F-06 |  |
| **P0-04** | **Tenancy.** Organisation → facility → membership. clinic_id on every clinic-owned row, enforced by an EF Core global query filter and Azure SQL row-level security (tenant set in SESSION_CONTEXT per request). One doctor can belong to several clinics through memberships. | MUST | — |  |
| **P0-05** | **Authorisation.** Role-permission matrix from Foundations (solo doctor, doctor, receptionist, nurse, practice admin, care coordinator, patient) checked server-side by ASP.NET Core authorisation policies on every endpoint, independently of the UI. Explicit 403 screens. | MUST | F-05 |  |
| **P0-06** | **Audit log.** Append-only record of every read and write of patient data, sign-in, export and permission change: actor, tenant, patient, purpose, time, IP. Stored in Azure SQL ledger tables so any tampering is detectable. | MUST | — |  |
| **P0-07** | **Design system in code.** Medvya MUI theme and tokens, clinical status primitives, component states and microcopy from Handoff; light theme; WCAG 2.2 AA base; English, Hindi and Arabic (RTL) string pipeline. | MUST | X-03 |  |
| **P0-08** | **Safety and compliance groundwork.** Threat model, data map, DPIA draft (DPDP), record-retention map per country, ADR-001 stack decision, ADR-002 launch market. | MUST | — |  |
| **P0-09** | **Database security baseline.** Entra-only database authentication, API connects with a managed identity (no passwords anywhere), separate least-privilege database users per module and for migrations, Always Encrypted on national ID and insurance member columns, dynamic data masking for support roles, TDE with customer-managed key. Details in section 7b. | MUST | — | ADDED v2 |
| **P0-10** | **Secure development and data classification.** Every field classified (public, internal, personal, sensitive health, national ID); synthetic-only test data policy; SECURITY.md and code review rules; privileged access through just-in-time elevation only; offline break-glass account. | MUST | — | ADDED v2 |

**Platform & non-functional**

- OWASP ASVS L2 used as the checklist from the first commit
- Structured logs with PHI redaction; telemetry processor drops request bodies and classified fields
- Daily encrypted backup + point-in-time restore enabled

**Exit criteria (release gate)**

- [ ] Clinical advisor walks all six journeys (X-03) and signs off the flows
- [ ] Restore from backup tested once and timed
- [ ] Cross-tenant read attempt blocked by RLS in automated test
- [ ] CI green on protected main; staging deploy from a tag

**Delivery package**

- Staging URL with seeded synthetic tenant
- ADR set, threat model, role matrix, data map
- R0 release notes

**Dependencies & risks**

- Azure subscription and launch region confirmed
- Founder decision on launch market (ADR-002)

**Not in this phase:** Any real patient data. Public website. Booking.


## P1 · Front desk and appointments MVP

- **Weeks:** Weeks 4–10 · **Release:** R1 · Front Desk
- **Delivered to:** Receptionists, doctors (schedule view) and owners at 2 design-partner clinics
- **Day one:** Register patients, book, reschedule and cancel appointments, check patients in, run the waiting room and send automatic confirmations and reminders.
- **Goal:** A clinic can run its entire appointment day in Medvya. This is the workflow to validate with real clinics before anything clinical is built on top.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Screens | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P1-01** | **Public site.** Landing for solo doctors and clinics, country and data-residency selector, trust centre, demo request. | SHOULD | F-01, F-02, F-07 |  |
| **P1-02** | **Clinic onboarding and settings.** Solo doctor and clinic modes; practice profile, locations, operating hours, holidays, notification preferences. | MUST | F-04, F-08 |  |
| **P1-03** | **Doctor and staff accounts.** Add doctor (licence number and country, signature, schedule), add staff with roles and scope, custom roles, invites. | MUST | F-09, F-10 |  |
| **P1-04** | **Schedules and availability.** Working hours, breaks, slot length per service, leave and schedule exceptions, time zones, per-location calendars. | MUST | P-04 |  |
| **P1-05** | **Patient registration.** India (ABHA optional, Aadhaar masked) and UAE (Emirates ID entered manually); guardian, emergency contact; duplicate warning while typing; merge review; patient directory and search. | MUST | P-02, P-03 |  |
| **P1-06** | **Booking.** Create, reschedule, cancel, no-show, walk-in, recurring and waitlist; day, week and list calendar views. | MUST | P-04, P-05 |  |
| **P1-07** | **No double booking.** Unique index on (doctor, location, slot start), booking inside a serializable transaction with an application lock per doctor-day, and a short slot hold. The frontend check is only a convenience. | MUST | — |  |
| **P1-08** | **Reception board and queue.** Check-in, nonclinical statuses, call or room patient, shared waiting room, multi-doctor overview, waiting-room TV display. | MUST | P-01, P-05, D-04 |  |
| **P1-09** | **Confirmations and reminders.** Email (Azure Communication Services) and SMS confirmations, 24 h and 2 h reminders, cancellations; retries and delivery status; notification centre. | MUST | D-03 |  |
| **P1-10** | **Practice access log.** Owner can see who opened which record and when. | MUST | F-12 |  |
| **P1-11** | **Staff lifecycle.** Offboarding removes access immediately and ends sessions; licence and registration expiry reminders; quarterly access review prompt for owners. | MUST | F-10 | ADDED v2 |
| **P1-12** | **Legal and consent at registration.** Terms of service, privacy notice, clinic data processing agreement, and separate patient consents for treatment, reminders and marketing, each versioned and recorded. | MUST | P-02, F-08 | ADDED v2 |

**Platform & non-functional**

- Booking API p95 < 300 ms; calendar first render < 2.5 s on a clinic PC over 4G
- Hangfire on Azure SQL for reminders; no Redis or Service Bus yet
- Mobile-responsive reception views (tablet at the desk)

**Exit criteria (release gate)**

- [ ] Both clinics run 2 consecutive weeks of real bookings without paper fallback
- [ ] 0 double bookings with 100 parallel attempts on one slot
- [ ] Median check-in ≤ 60 s for a returning patient
- [ ] ≥ 98% reminders delivered; failures visible to reception
- [ ] No open high or critical security findings

**Delivery package**

- Production tenant per clinic
- 30-minute reception training and a one-page desk card
- WhatsApp/phone support channel with named contact
- Baseline metrics captured (no-shows, check-in time)

**Dependencies & risks**

- Privacy notice and consent wording reviewed for DPDP / UAE
- India DLT SMS sender ID and templates registered
- Two partner clinics signed with a pilot agreement

**Not in this phase:** Clinical notes, prescriptions, billing, AI, patient portal.


## P2 · Doctor workspace and EMR core

- **Weeks:** Weeks 9–15 · **Release:** R2 · Consult
- **Delivered to:** Doctors and nurses at the 2 partner clinics
- **Day one:** Open Doctor Today, see the patient chart, record vitals, write and sign a note, and print a prescription, without AI.
- **Goal:** A doctor completes a full visit, from chart to signed note and prescription, in Medvya. This is also the fallback that AI must never break.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Screens | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P2-01** | **Doctor Today.** Today’s schedule, patient flags, pending notes, inbox counts; privacy-safe global search. | MUST | D-01, D-02 |  |
| **P2-02** | **Patient 360.** Banner with identity and allergies always visible; problems, medicines, history, vitals trends, one timeline with source labels, documents. | MUST | E-01, E-02, E-03 |  |
| **P2-03** | **Nurse intake.** Vitals, allergy verification, patient-reported medicines, handoff to doctor. | MUST | N-01 |  |
| **P2-04** | **Consultation note.** Chief complaint, SOAP and specialty templates, ICD-10 coding, medicine reconciliation (keep, stop, change). | MUST | E-04, E-07 |  |
| **P2-05** | **Sign and finalise.** Signed notes are immutable; changes only by dated addendum; print and PDF. | MUST | E-06 |  |
| **P2-06** | **Prescriptions and orders.** Country formulary (India Schedule H/H1/X, UAE drug codes), dose builder, allergy and interaction checks, add medicine, multilingual printed Rx, investigation orders, referrals in and out. | MUST | E-05, E-10, E-11, F-13, E-09 |  |
| **P2-07** | **Documents.** Private blob storage, malware scan, secure viewer with time-limited links, original file always kept. | MUST | E-03 |  |
| **P2-08** | **Clinical safety case.** Hazard log for every clinical feature (wrong patient, missed allergy, wrong dose, lost result), mitigations tied to tests, and a named clinical safety reviewer who signs each release from P2 onward. | MUST | — | ADDED v2 |

**Platform & non-functional**

- Clinical data legal review complete before first real note
- Print layouts: A4/A5 Rx, 200% zoom, screen-reader labels on clinical controls
- Prescription PDF rendered server-side and stored with hash

**Exit criteria (release gate)**

- [ ] ≥ 20 real visits per pilot doctor signed in Medvya
- [ ] Allergy and interaction checks fire in 100% of seeded conflict tests
- [ ] Signed notes cannot be edited (only addendum), proven by automated test
- [ ] Each doctor approves their own Rx print layout

**Delivery package**

- 30-minute doctor and nurse training
- Note template pack per specialty at the partner clinics
- R2 release notes and known-issues list

**Dependencies & risks**

- Formulary data source per country licensed or curated
- Doctor licence verification process defined

**Not in this phase:** AI drafting, billing, results inbox, e-prescription submission to regulators.


## P3 · AI-drafted notes under clinician review

- **Weeks:** Weeks 13–20 · **Release:** R3 · Scribe
- **Delivered to:** 5–10 opt-in clinicians under clinical review
- **Day one:** Record a consented consultation on phone or desktop, review a draft note with evidence links, correct it and sign.
- **Goal:** Medvya drafts the note from the conversation; the doctor checks each statement against its source and signs. Nothing AI-generated is saved without explicit approval.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Screens | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P3-01** | **Recording consent.** Per-encounter consent separate from treatment consent; declined consent goes straight to a manual note; clinic consent templates and recording policy; consent revoked mid-visit stops capture. | MUST | A-02, H-09, A-09 |  |
| **P3-02** | **Capture.** Phone (mobile web) or desktop microphone; visible timer, pause and consent indicator; encrypted chunked upload with resume; battery and network warnings. | MUST | A-03, A-06, X-01 |  |
| **P3-03** | **Transcription and speakers.** In-region Azure AI Speech; provisional speaker labels the doctor confirms; overlap and uncertain-speaker handling with no identity asserted. | MUST | A-04, A-10 |  |
| **P3-04** | **Draft note with evidence.** Every statement links to transcript segments; unknown fields left blank, never guessed; no invented negatives, medicines or doses; template switch; clinician edits tracked. | MUST | A-05 |  |
| **P3-05** | **Pre-visit brief.** Verified chart facts kept visibly separate from AI summary. | SHOULD | A-01 |  |
| **P3-06** | **Safety states.** Emergency-symptom warning (no autonomous triage); AI unavailable → editable manual note with no data loss; wrong-patient suspicion locks the session. | MUST | A-08, A-06 |  |
| **P3-07** | **AI worker.** .NET 10 worker service on Azure Service Bus using Microsoft.Extensions.AI; no direct database access, scoped short-lived inputs, versioned prompts and models, de-identified evaluation set run in CI before any prompt change; audio deleted per retention policy. | MUST | — |  |
| **P3-08** | **Dictation.** Doctor dictates sections of the note; same review-and-approve rule. | SHOULD | — |  |

**Platform & non-functional**

- Draft ready ≤ 60 s (p50) after recording stops
- No training on customer data without separate lawful basis
- AI vendor DPA and regional processing confirmed per country

**Exit criteria (release gate)**

- [ ] 0 fabricated medicines or doses across the evaluation set
- [ ] ≥ 80% of drafts signed with only minor edits (clinician rated)
- [ ] Consent recorded for 100% of recordings; declined path tested
- [ ] Clinician trust survey and note time compared with P2 baseline

**Delivery package**

- AI safety card for clinicians
- Waiting-room consent notice in English, Hindi and Arabic
- Evaluation report and AI incident procedure

**Dependencies & risks**

- Azure OpenAI / Speech availability in Central India and UAE North
- Legal review of recording consent in each market

**Not in this phase:** Wearable clip, earpiece assistant, Arabic–Hindi–Malayalam mixed-language notes (P6).


## P4 · Billing, care follow-up and patient portal

- **Weeks:** Weeks 17–26 · **Release:** R4 · Clinic Ops
- **Delivered to:** Clinic owners and admins, care coordinators and the clinics’ patients
- **Day one:** Bill and collect payment, close the cash drawer, track every result and follow-up to closure, and let patients book and see their records.
- **Goal:** The clinic runs its money and its follow-ups in Medvya, and patients can serve themselves.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Screens | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P4-01** | **Services and fees.** Price lists with GST/SAC (India), VAT/CPT and payer price lists (UAE), packages. | MUST | F-11 |  |
| **P4-02** | **Invoicing.** Charge capture, invoice, receipt, tax invoice, credit note, advance receipt, refund; legal numbering per country; A5 and 80 mm thermal print. | MUST | P-06, P-15 |  |
| **P4-03** | **Payments.** Cash, UPI, card and advance; split and partial; Razorpay (India), Network International or Stripe (UAE); provider tokenisation only. | MUST | P-10 |  |
| **P4-04** | **Packages, dues and close.** Packages and session redemption, dues and ageing, patient statement, cash reconciliation, day-end close with denominations, shift report, doctor revenue and payout. | MUST | P-11, P-12, P-07, P-13, P-09 |  |
| **P4-05** | **Closed-loop results and care.** Results inbox with identity match and acknowledgement; care plans with owners and due dates; contact log; overdue escalation. A sent reminder never closes a task. | MUST | C-01, C-05, C-02, C-03, C-04 |  |
| **P4-06** | **Clinic messages.** Patient ↔ clinic inbox with AI reply draft that staff approve. | SHOULD | C-06 |  |
| **P4-07** | **Patient portal.** Home, released visit summaries, prescriptions, records and labs, booking and reschedule, consent and privacy controls, caregiver proxy; Arabic RTL. | MUST | R-01, R-02, R-03, R-04 |  |
| **P4-08** | **Doctor discovery.** Public doctor and clinic profiles with live availability, indexed for search. | SHOULD | N-02 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P4-09** | **WhatsApp.** Reminders and confirmations in English, Arabic and Hindi; one-tap reschedule; “doctor running late” broadcast; opt-in records. | MUST | N-03 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P4-10** | **Clinic reports.** Appointments, no-shows, revenue, follow-up completion, note time saved. | MUST | H-07 |  |

**Platform & non-functional**

- Money stored as integer minor units; payment webhooks idempotent
- Portal p95 < 2 s on mobile; OTP sign-in for patients
- Released-result rules: doctor controls what patients see and when

**Exit criteria (release gate)**

- [ ] Cash close balances with zero unexplained variance for 10 consecutive days
- [ ] Invoice formats reviewed by a chartered accountant (India) / tax adviser (UAE)
- [ ] 0 abnormal results unacknowledged > 72 h during pilot
- [ ] ≥ 30% of bookings confirmed by patients via portal or WhatsApp

**Delivery package**

- Billing setup service (price list import)
- Owner dashboard walkthrough
- Patient-facing help pages in three languages

**Dependencies & risks**

- Payment gateway merchant approvals (can take weeks)
- WhatsApp Business API template approval

**Not in this phase:** Insurance claims and eligibility (P5). Teleconsultation (P8).


## P5 · Commercial launch v1.0

- **Weeks:** Weeks 24–32 · **Release:** R5 · v1.0 GA
- **Delivered to:** First paying clinic (week 29), then the first 5 paying clinics in the launch market
- **Day one:** Switch from the old system without closing, with history migrated, insurance checked at the desk and a paid subscription.
- **Goal:** Everything a clinic owner needs to say yes: their data moved, no downtime, regulator-ready, learnable in one shift, and no lock-in.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Screens | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P5-01** | **Migration pipeline.** Read-only connection (self-hosted integration runtime, no open ports), AI-proposed column and code mappings approved by a person, dry-run report signed by the owner, day-one load, change-data-capture parallel run for 1–2 weeks, background backfill. Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, CSV/Excel. | MUST | N-04 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P5-02** | **Data quality.** Problems grouped by type and fixed by rule; duplicate scoring incl. Arabic–English name spellings; every imported value badged with source; merges and fixes reversible. | MUST | N-05 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P5-03** | **Insurance.** Live eligibility and co-pay estimate; pre-authorisation, claims, resubmission, remittance matching. India TPA/PMJAY/CGHS; UAE eClaimLink and Shafafiya. | MUST | P-08, P-14 |  |
| **P5-04** | **UAE market pack.** Emirates ID card-reader check-in (< 30 s); health-exchange pull and push for the launch emirate; regulator e-prescription and e-sick leave. | MUST | N-06, N-07, N-09 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P5-05** | **Outside records.** Patient uploads PDFs or photos before the visit; extraction into trends marked “Unverified · patient upload” until the doctor accepts. | SHOULD | N-08 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P5-06** | **Voice appointment assistant v1.** Answers the clinic number after hours and when lines are busy; books, moves and cancels from the live calendar; verifies identity before sharing details; no medical advice; hands over to staff with transcript. | SHOULD | N-10 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P5-07** | **Medvya subscription.** Plans, trial, subscription invoices to clinics (GST/VAT), seat counts, dunning. | MUST | N-11 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P5-08** | **Platform operations console.** Tenant catalogue, onboarding automation, feature flags per tenant, time-boxed support access that is audited and visible to the clinic. | MUST | N-12 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P5-09** | **Adoption and exit.** In-app guides per role, help centre, feedback, status page; full clinic data export in FHIR and CSV. | MUST | N-13, N-14 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P5-10** | **Hardening.** External penetration test, DR drill, accessibility audit, load test, dark and high-contrast themes. | MUST | X-02 |  |
| **P5-11** | **Security operations.** Incident response plan with breach notification steps for DPDP and UAE regulators, Defender and Sentinel alerts routed to on-call, Customer Lockbox, vulnerability disclosure policy, ADHICS control evidence, ISO 27001 readiness gap assessment. | MUST | — | ADDED v2 |
| **P5-12** | **Retention, deletion and data rights.** Scheduled jobs apply each country’s record-retention rule; audio deleted on schedule; patient access, correction and erasure requests handled for clinics (full enterprise workflow H-10 in P7). | MUST | H-10 | ADDED v2 |

**Platform & non-functional**

- RPO ≤ 15 min, RTO ≤ 4 h, rehearsed
- 99.5% monthly availability target with status page
- Support: first response < 4 business hours

**Exit criteria (release gate)**

- [ ] First paying clinic cuts over without closing (week 29)
- [ ] Migration dry-run report signed before load
- [ ] Pen test: no open high or critical findings
- [ ] 30 days at ≥ 99.5% availability before GA (week 32)

**Delivery package**

- Signed order form and SLA
- Migration report and go-live runbook
- Role training (30 min each) and in-app guides
- v1.0 release notes

**Dependencies & risks**

- Regulator onboarding and conformance testing (Malaffi, NABIDH, Riayati, eClaimLink, Shafafiya) controls UAE dates; India launch can proceed independently
- Card-reader hardware sourcing

**Not in this phase:** Other two UAE exchanges, ABHA consent records, outbound voice calls (P6/P8).


## P6 · Wearable capture and advanced AI

- **Weeks:** Weeks 33–42 (after hardware is stable) · **Release:** R6 · Clip
- **Delivered to:** Doctors issued a Medvya clip, and their practice admins
- **Day one:** Pair a clip, record without a phone on the desk, get mixed-language notes and a private earpiece assistant.
- **Goal:** Hands-free capture and multilingual AI once the phone-first flow is trusted.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Screens | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P6-01** | **Clip lifecycle.** Pairing code, self-test, battery and health, encrypted offline buffer, firmware updates, loss/theft revoke. | MUST | W-01, W-02, W-03 |  |
| **P6-02** | **Private voice assistant.** Earpiece-only answers to the doctor; never spoken to the patient. | SHOULD | A-07 |  |
| **P6-03** | **Multilingual notes.** Arabic, English, Hindi and Malayalam including mixed-language consultations; original and translation side by side. | MUST | A-04 |  |
| **P6-04** | **Outbound voice.** Reminder and recall calls for patients without WhatsApp; waitlist fill from cancellations. | SHOULD | N-10 |  |
| **P6-05** | **Stronger AI QA.** Per-language evaluation sets, clinician trust metrics, red-team prompts on uploaded documents. | MUST | — |  |

**Platform & non-functional**

- Visible recording light on device; start/stop bound to an encounter
- Signed firmware and secure update path

**Exit criteria (release gate)**

- [ ] Device, consent, offline and overlap test suites pass
- [ ] Battery lasts a full clinic day
- [ ] Revoke takes effect in < 1 minute

**Delivery package**

- Device kit and quick-start
- Fleet guide for admins

**Dependencies & risks**

- Hardware partner and certification
- Language model quality per language

**Not in this phase:** Autonomous triage or diagnosis.


## P7 · Hospital enterprise and integrations

- **Weeks:** Weeks 36–60 · **Release:** R7 · Enterprise
- **Delivered to:** First hospital customer: IT, administrators and clinicians
- **Day one:** Connect Medvya to the hospital HIS, sign in with hospital SSO, and write signed notes back with conflicts surfaced.
- **Goal:** Medvya works inside a hospital that keeps its own system of record.

| ID | Requirement | Priority | Screens | Flags |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P7-01** | **Record authority.** Per facility: Medvya or external HIS holds the official chart; synced copies labelled. | MUST | H-08 |  |
| **P7-02** | **Organisation.** Facilities, departments, multi-location administration. | MUST | H-02 |  |
| **P7-03** | **SSO and provisioning.** SAML/OIDC SSO, SCIM, department and facility role grants. | MUST | H-03 |  |
| **P7-04** | **Integrations.** HL7 v2 and FHIR interfaces, write-back queue with conflict and retry, lab feeds (HL7 ORU), imaging viewer links. | MUST | H-01, H-04, N-15 | DESIGN NEEDED |
| **P7-05** | **Governance.** Audit log and break-glass review, retention and residency policies, data subject requests and export, full analytics. | MUST | H-05, H-06, H-10, H-07 |  |
| **P7-06** | **Dedicated deployment.** Per-hospital stamp, customer-managed keys, private links (Azure Architecture stage 4). | MUST | — |  |

**Platform & non-functional**

- SIEM export, privileged access review
- Move from App Service to AKS when stamp count or isolation requires it

**Exit criteria (release gate)**

- [ ] Integration contract and security review passed
- [ ] Write-back success ≥ 99% with every conflict visible
- [ ] Hospital clinical sign-off

**Delivery package**

- Integration specification and runbook
- Security evidence pack

**Dependencies & risks**

- Hospital procurement and HIS vendor cooperation

**Not in this phase:** Full hospital inventory, ERP.
